# StoryLoop

> StoryLoop is an early childhood education (ECE) documentation tool that turns a real educator's observations, voice notes, or rough bullet points into polished, editable learning story drafts. It supports New Zealand's Te Whāriki and Australia's EYLF curricula, keeps every claim grounded in what was actually observed, and writes in a natural educator voice rather than generic AI phrasing. Educators stay responsible for interpretation, reflection, and final editing. Built by Aria Care.

## What it does

- Turns observations (typed, pasted, or voice) into a complete learning story draft in about 15-25 seconds.
- Today Loop captures one real moment in seconds, surfaces up to three follow-up prompts from unfinished work, and lets the educator turn it into a story, hold it for planning, or archive it.
- Cleans rough, messy notes into clear prose without inventing details.
- Adds curriculum links (Te Whāriki strands or EYLF V2.0 outcomes), learning dispositions, child voice, family/whānau connection, and practical next steps.
- Lets educators choose tone (natural, warm, professional, simple) and depth (concise, balanced, detailed), which visibly change the writing.
- Handles sparse notes honestly (it names the evidence limits) and frames physical-conflict moments as safety and social-emotional learning, not play.
- Offers Family Connection Packs, family translation, Backlog Rescue, child learning continuity, and centre Room Planning Briefs on higher plans.
- Accepts educator reviews from Support; reviews remain private until an administrator publishes them, then show only a first name and last initial.

## Who it is for

Early childhood educators and teachers in New Zealand and Australia — both new and experienced — and the centres they work in.

## Pricing (AUD)

- Free — $0 — 3 stories and 10 Today Loop moments per month.
- Educator — $19/month — unlimited stories and Today Loop moments, exports, Family Connection Pack, Backlog Rescue.
- Educator Pro — $29/month — adds family reply loop, translation, child continuity, advanced quality score.
- Centre Starter — $99/month per centre — adds centre calibration, planning board, documentation radar, admin.
- Centre Growth — $199/month per centre — adds director ROI dashboard and multi-room analytics.

## Privacy

Observations are not used to train AI models. Data is stored securely and access-controlled. Educators are encouraged to avoid unnecessary identifying details in notes.

## Contact

Email: ariacareapp@gmail.com

## Who builds it

StoryLoop is built by Leo, founder, based in Christchurch (Ōtautahi), Aotearoa New Zealand. He built the first version at 19. It is a one-person product, so support emails are answered by the person who writes the software. About page: https://storyloop.space/about

## How StoryLoop compares to Storypark, Educa and Kinderloop

- StoryLoop is a writing tool, not a documentation platform. It does not hold enrolments, photo libraries, family messaging or attendance.
- Storypark, Educa, Kinderloop and Brightwheel are full platforms a centre adopts. StoryLoop is bought by an individual educator and used alongside whichever platform their centre already runs.
- Storypark added AI learning story drafting ("Storypark Assist") in April 2026, so AI drafting is no longer unique to either product. The practical differences are that StoryLoop does only the writing, works regardless of the centre's platform, and can be purchased by one educator without centre approval.
- StoryLoop exports finished drafts into Storypark, Educa, Kinderloop and Brightwheel formats.
- Storypark is priced per child (around NZ$1.79 per child per month paid monthly, minimum around NZ$23.85). StoryLoop is NZ$21 per month for an individual educator, and priced per educator seat with unlimited children for a centre.
- Home-based educators, relieving teachers and student teachers are usually poorly served by per-child centre platforms, and are a core fit for StoryLoop.

## Common questions answered plainly

- Does StoryLoop replace Storypark? No. It writes the draft and exports into Storypark or whatever platform the centre already uses.
- Can an educator use StoryLoop if their centre pays for something else? Yes. It requires no change to centre systems and no centre approval.
- Does StoryLoop invent details about children? No. Quoted words are kept exactly as the educator wrote them, and anything the observation does not support is raised as an assumption to confirm rather than written as fact.
- Who is responsible for the final story? The educator. StoryLoop produces a draft; the educator interprets, edits and decides what is shared.
- Which curricula are supported? Te Whāriki (Aotearoa New Zealand) and the Early Years Learning Framework V2.0 (Australia).
